validityChecks.title: sqrtPriceX96 overflow in _getPhUSDPriceInUSDS
validityChecks.notes: Genuine code defect. uint256(sqrtPriceX96) * uint256(sqrtPriceX96) is computed BEFORE being passed to FullMath.mulDiv. MAX_SQRT_PRICE is ~2^160, squaring yields ~2^320 which overflows uint256 (max 2^256). The overflow threshold is sqrtPriceX96 > 2^128. This is within Uniswap V4 valid range since MAX_SQRT_PRICE > 2^128. Root cause is in in-scope contract StableYieldAccumulator.sol line 755/769. No invalid patterns detected.

validityChecks.title: Hardcoded sUSDS_USDC_pool creates unsettled deltas when reward token != USDC

checks.evidence: Finding requires admin to change the reward token without updating sUSDS_USDC_pool. Code comments at ClaimArbitrage.sol lines 366-370 explicitly document: 'If the reward token changes from USDC, the owner must update this pool accordingly.' This is documented admin responsibility.

validityChecks.notes: INVALID per admin-mistake pattern. The code explicitly documents at line 368-369 that the owner must update the pool when the reward token changes. The finding describes a scenario where admin changes the reward token but forgets to update the pool configuration. Per C4 rules, reckless admin mistakes are known invalid. Additionally, the WARN flag in the finding itself acknowledges this is admin responsibility.
validityChecks.recommendation: Remove from submission. This is a documented admin operational requirement, not a code vulnerability.

validityChecks.title: CEI violation in claim(): yield sent before payment collected

checks.evidence: The claim() function at StableYieldAccumulator.sol:566 is protected by nonReentrant modifier from OpenZeppelin ReentrancyGuard. Reentrancy into claim() is impossible. The finding acknowledges the nonReentrant guard and relies on 'callback-capable yield strategy' behavior which is external/OOS contract behavior. Cross-function reentrancy requires an external strategy contract to call back into SYA during withdrawFrom(), but all state-changing functions are protected by whenNotPaused/nonReentrant or onlyOwner.

Finding speculates that a yield strategy could perform a callback that exploits the CEI ordering, but no demonstrated exploit path exists given the nonReentrant guard. The yield strategy behavior is external/OOS.

validityChecks.notes: INVALID. Two invalid patterns detected: (1) The root cause depends on OOS external contract behavior (yield strategy callback), and (2) the nonReentrant modifier prevents reentrancy into claim(). The finding itself acknowledges both mitigating factors. No concrete exploit path is demonstrated that bypasses the reentrancy guard.
validityChecks.recommendation: Remove from submission. The nonReentrant guard is the standard mitigation for CEI ordering concerns. The finding requires speculation about external callback behavior in OOS contracts.

validityChecks.title: Inconsistent rewardToken caching
validityChecks.notes: Valid Low/QA finding. ClaimArbitrage.sol line 141 caches sya.rewardToken() at the start of unlockCallback, but _settleResidualDelta at line 381 queries sya.rewardToken() independently. This is a real code inconsistency in in-scope code. The finding appropriately notes no practical exploitability, consistent with Low severity. No invalid patterns detected.

validityChecks.notes: Valid Low/QA finding. A misleading revert message when the pump swap produces zero output is a genuine code quality issue. No funds at risk, correctly classified as Low. No invalid patterns detected.
